newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU calls for consultations with Japan on shipping.
newsitem.headline: EU calls for consultations with Japan on shipping.

text.p: The European Commission on Monday called for World Trade Organisation consultations with Japan over maritime policy to make ports more accessible to foreign shippers.
It said in statement that requirements for foreign shippers to consult Japanese harbour authorities in advance on even minor changes to schedules meant large supplementary costs.
"Today's action follows diplomatic efforts which have failed to bring about any fundamental restructuring of the Japanese consultation system," the statement said.

The Commission said Japan's Harbour Transportation Association (JHTA) controlled loading and unloading of all ships in Japanese harbours. If shippers want to make any change to a schedule, prior approval from the JHTA is required.
"This de facto monopoly on stevedoring in Japan gives JHTA tremendous power over shipping lines. Prices of port operations in Japan are well above international levels," it said.
The Commission said bilateral diplomatic approaches over several years had failed to solve the issue.
